question: Does a third anchor (over-determined joint BVP) lower the fast-seed ω-dir noise floor and collapse the winding multiplicity?
hypothesis: A third intermediate anchor (a) averages endpoint noise down below the 1.25° gate and (b) pins the winding so long baselines no longer alias.
narrative_md: Split result: Q2 (multiplicity) confirmed decisively — the third anchor collapses the fast-seed winding ladder 26→1 (119), 4→1 (SAM 103), and rescues an aliased long baseline 39.6°→1.38°. Q1 (noise floor) refuted on the binding fast seed — joint tracks 2-pt (1.49° vs 1.57°), both clearing 1.25° only at σ_q≲2.0°. The third anchor is a disambiguator, not a noise-reducer. Perturbed-truth anchors → not blind.
